what_it_does: Sparse matrix operations — multiplying matrices where most entries are zero and only the non-zero values are stored — are important in AI and graph computation, but the non-zero values are scattered unpredictably, making it hard to keep all processing units busy. HBM (high-bandwidth memory) is a type of fast memory chip stacked directly on a processor, divided into multiple independent channels that can transfer data in parallel. The problem is that if the non-zero values of the matrix are statically assigned to channels at the start, some channels end up with much more work than others, leaving processing units idle. Chason introduces dynamic cross-channel migration: at runtime, when one channel runs out of work, the system moves non-zero data from a busier channel to it, balancing the load on the fly. This is implemented on a real programmable chip (FPGA, a reconfigurable hardware device) and evaluated on standard sparse matrix benchmark collections.
